pages.title: VOWEL REVIEW
pages.subtitle: SHORT & LONG SOUNDS · a, e, i, o, u, y

blocks.text: VOWEL REVIEW  SHORT & LONG SOUNDS

SHORT VOWELS: a, e, i, o, u — as in cat, bed, pig, hot, cup

LONG VOWELS: a, e, i, o, u — as in cake, tree, bike, boat, cube

VOWEL Y: Y acts as a vowel at the end of words — fly, baby, gym

READ ALOUD: cat, cake, bed, tree, pig, bike, hot, boat, cup, cube

Notice the difference between short and long vowel sounds.
FINAL PATTERN -ZE  AS IN FREEZE

THE PATTERN: Words ending in -ze have a long vowel sound before the final z.

EXAMPLES: freeze (long e), breeze (long e), sneeze (long e)

WHY: The silent e makes the vowel long.

READ ALOUD: freeze, breeze, sneeze, blaze, doze

The silent e keeps the vowel long.
FINAL PATTERN -AGE  AS IN MESSAGE

THE PATTERN: Words ending in -age usually have a schwa sound (/j/) at the end.

EXAMPLES: message (mes·sage), village (vil·lage), package (pack·age)

WHY: The -age ending is common in nouns.

READ ALOUD: message, village, package, courage, garage

The -age ending sounds like "ij".
DIPHTHONGS  OI/OY, OU/OW, AU/AW

WHAT IS A DIPHTHONG? Two vowels that glide together to form one sound.

oi/oy: coin, boy — mouth glides

ou/ow: house, cow — mouth glides

au/aw: haul, paw — mouth glides

READ ALOUD: coin, boy, house, cow, haul, paw

Vowels glide together to make one sound.
SUFFIXES -TION / -SION  AS IN ACTION & VISION

-tion: action, motion, nation, station

-sion: vision, division, decision, confusion

HOW TO REMEMBER: -tion is more common; -sion is used after certain roots.

READ ALOUD: action, vision, nation, division, decision

These suffixes turn verbs into nouns.
SILENT LETTERS  KN, WR, MB, GH

kn: silent k — knee, know, knife

wr: silent w — write, wrist, wrap

mb: silent b — comb, thumb, climb

gh: silent gh — light, night, high

READ ALOUD: knee, know, write, wrist, comb, light

Remember: one letter stays silent.
SOFT C & G REVIEW  CENT, CITY, GIANT, GYM

SOFT C: When c is followed by e, i, y → /s/ (cent, city, cycle)

SOFT G: When g is followed by e, i, y → /j/ (giant, gym, gem)

HARD C/G: Before a, o, u → /k/ and /g/ (cat, go, cup)

READ ALOUD: cent, city, cycle, giant, gym, gem

e, i, y makes c and g soft.
HIGH-FREQUENCY WORDS  READ & SPELL

WHAT ARE THEY? Words that appear often in text and may not follow phonics rules.

HOW TO LEARN: Read, spell, and use in sentences daily.

READ ALOUD: the, of, and, to, in, said, were, they, have

Practice these every day.
